identity.title: Si-bearing Molecules Toward IRC+10216: ALMA Unveils the Molecular Envelope of CWLeo

paper_type_evidence.quote: We report the detection of SiS rotational lines in high-vibrational states as well as SiO and SiC$_2$ lines in their ground vibrational state toward IRC+10216 during the Atacama Large Millimeter Array Cycle 0.

evidence.quote: The continuum comes from a point-like source located at $\alpha$=9$^{\mathrm{h}}$47$^{\mathrm{m}}$57$^{\mathrm{s}}$446 and $\delta$=13$^{\circ}$16$^{'}$43$''$86 (J2000)
considering a distance of $\sim$130 pc to the star from us (cite: gro12)

question.value: What are the spatial distributions and excitation conditions of Si-bearing molecules (SiS, SiO, SiC2) in the envelope of IRC+10216?

evidence.quote: We analyze the excitation conditions of the vibrationally excited SiS using the population diagram technique, and we use a large velocity gradient model to compare with the observations.
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2011.0.00229.S .
IRC+10216 was observed in the frequency range 255.3 to 274.8 GHz (band 6) covered by four different setups with a bandwidth of $\sim$5 GHz

frequencies_and_spectral_setup.value: channel spacing 0.49 MHz, effective resolution 0.98 MHz, ~5 GHz per setup

evidence.quote: a channel spacing of 0.49 MHz and an effective resolution of 0.98 MHz
We detected emission of SiS $J$=15 – 14 lines of vibrationally excited states, from v=0 up to v=7, and tentatively of v=8, 9 and 10.
We also detected emission of SiO $J$=6 – 5 (v=0–2), $^{29}$SiO $J$=6 – 5 (v=0)

baselines.value: up to 402 m, shortest ~20 m, sixteen antennas

evidence.quote: The observations were performed using sixteen antennas covering baselines up to 402 m
that allowed us to obtain an angular resolution of $\sim$0.6$''$
which allow us to recover structures with a size up to $\lesssim$12$''$

time_on_source.value: Two runs of 72 min each, 26 min on source

evidence.quote: Two runs of 72 minutes each were performed, of which 26 minutes correspond to correlations on source.
The observations were carried out with ALMA[^1] between 2012 April 8 and 23 during Cycle 0.

what.value: SiS collisional data, extrapolated to high rovibrational levels

evidence.quote: The SiS collisional data were taken from (cite: tob08) and extrapolated to high rovibrational levels.
The dipole moment function used for SiS was determined semiempirically by (cite: LopezPineiro87)

evidence.quote: We adopted a distance to the star of $\sim$130 pc, an effective temperature of $\sim$2330 K and a stellar radius of $\sim$4$\times$10$^{13}$ cm

pipeline_or_manual.value: Calibration with CASA; details in Cernicharo et al. 2013

evidence.quote: The calibration of the data was performed using CASA[^2] and data analysis with GILDAS[^3].

evidence.quote: We modified the H$_2$ density, decreasing it by a factor $\sim$2, as described in (cite: cer13)

analysis_steps.goal: Rotational diagram of vibrationally excited SiS

method.value: Rotational diagram technique on spectra at stellar position; two linear fits (v=0-2 and v=3-7), v>=8 excluded

evidence.quote: We considered two different linear trends for the observational data: one for the transitions with E$_{up}$$\lesssim$2500 K (i.e. v=0, 1 and 2), and a different trend for the rest (i.e. v=3–7).

evidence.quote: We used a large velocity gradient (LVG) code to model the SiS emission (cite: cer12).

validation.value: Compared Tvib and column density with rotational diagram

evidence.quote: we obtain a good agreement with the vibrational temperature derived from the vibrational diagram and moderate discrepancies with the total column density within a factor of $\sim$2

analysis_steps.goal: SiS potential energy function and dipole matrix elements

method.value: Fit of BO potential with BOB corrections to 2863 line positions; Schrödinger equation solved variationally

evidence.quote: The fit to the potential energy function was performed using the Levenberg–Marquardt algorithm (cite: Levenberg44; Marquardt63) to minimize the $\chi^{2}$ function

fitting.value: Levenberg-Marquardt chi2 minimization, weights by squared experimental uncertainties

evidence.loc: SiS potential energy function and vibrational dipole moment
evidence.quote: The fit to the potential energy function was performed using the Levenberg–Marquardt algorithm (cite: Levenberg44; Marquardt63) to minimize the $\chi^{2}$ function, with the line positions weighted by the square of the experimental uncertainties.

validation.value: Compared with Lopez-Pineiro et al. 1987 for v<=4: excellent agreement

evidence.quote: The agreement between our calculations and those of (cite: LopezPineiro87) for v$\le$4 is excellent.

findings_qualitative.value: SiS emission is compact; SiO and SiC2 more extended; SiC2 shows a ring at ~10-11" probably partly filtered

evidence.quote: The spatial distribution of these molecules shows compact emission for SiS and a more extended emission for SiO and SiC$_2$

claims.hypothesis: Vibrationally excited SiS lines arise from the innermost hot envelope
claims.experiment: Line widths and rotational diagrams of SiS v=0-7
claims.result: FWHM decreases with increasing Eup; higher Tvib for high-v lines
claims.finding: High-v lines are excited close to the photosphere

evidence.quote: The FWHM of the lines measured from the spectra at the stellar position decreases with increasing upper level energy

claims.experiment: Two LVG models compared with rotational diagram
claims.result: Tvib agrees, column densities differ by ~2
claims.finding: Discrepancy may be due to optically thick lines and beam dilution

evidence.quote: We found moderate discrepancies between the observations and the models that could be explained if SiS lines detected are optically thick.

limitations_admitted.value: Ring structure of SiC2 probably filtered by shortest baselines; poor uv coverage and sidelobes for setups 3-5

evidence.quote: Although, this ringlike structure is probably filtered in our data given the shortest baselines used.

referee_caveats_inferred: Rotational diagram fit uncertainties and values not given
Maser nature of v=0 and optical thickness undermine low-v fit
Tentative lines v>=8 may be blended
